body.p: I. Introduction

The undersigned thanks Examiner Yankey for review and consideration of the present Application. In response to the Office Action of December 22, 2023 ("Office Action"), the undersigned submits the present amendment and remarks ("Response").

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 1 and 4-16 will be pending in this application. Claims 1 and 4-16 have been amended, claims 2, 3, 17, and 18 have been canceled. No new have been added. No new matter is added. Applicant has also amended the
specification to fix minor typographical errors in reference numbering of footrest from 109 to 209.
Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.
II. Drawing Objections

The drawings are objected to as the wall of claim 6 is allegedly not shown. Applicant clarifies that upper and lower walls 225, 227 of console 203 are shown in Fig. 4. In Figs. 1 to 3, a seat 210 is shown in second position in which seat pan 219 is arranged contiguously with footrest 209, as per amended claim 1 and in which walls 225 and 227 do not enclose the side of the seat 210 so that a passenger can access the seat 210 from the aisle when the seat is in the second position. Hence, a person of ordinary skill in the art can readily find support in the drawings. Accordingly, Applicant requests withdrawal of drawing objections.
III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 112

Claims 6-10 and 17-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite. Applicant has amended the claims to address the 112(b) issues and further clarify the 112(b) issues as follows:
Claim 1 now recites that the seat is movable from a first position to a second position. Therefore, there is antecedent basis for these terms recited by claim 6.

The Examiner has understood the "first position" to refer to an upright position of the seat and the "second position" to be a lie flat position of the seat. This understanding is incorrect. Applicant clarifies that claim 1 does not recite a lie flat position of the seat.

Amended claim 1 recites that "the seat is movable in the upright sitting configuration from a first position in which the seat pan is spaced apart from the footrest to a second position in which the seat pan arranged contiguously with the footrest". This statement is believed to be clear.

For example, in the embodiment shown in Figs 1 to 3 the seat 110 is in the first position and the seat 210 is in the second position. In the first position a wall formed by the console 103 blocks access to the seat 110 from the aisle 600. In the second position the wall formed by the console does not block the seat 210 (see also page 8, lines 19 to 26 of the application as filed).
Claim 1 now recites a second position so there is antecedent basis for this term in claim 7.
Applicant has rewritten claim 17 in independent form rendering the objection moot.
Claim 18 is cancelled rendering the objection moot.
For the aforementioned reasons, Applicant requests reconsideration and withdrawal of Section 112(b) rejections.
IV. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. " 102 & 103

Claims 1-2, 4-10, and 17 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 10,501,188 B2 to Nicholas et al. ("Nicholas"). Claims 3 and 18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, as applied to claim 1 above. Claims 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, as applied to claim 1 above in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,794,902 B2 to Pothier ("Pothier"). Claims 11-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Pothier, as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0126671 Al to Guering ("Guering"). Claims 14-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas, as applied to

claim 1 above, in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2017/0283064 Al to Robinson ("Robinson"). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections and submits that all the pending claims are patentable.

Independent claim 1 has been amended solely to expedite prosecution of this case. Claim 1, as amended, recites inter alia that the seat is movable to a (second) position which the seat pan is arranged contiguously with the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together form a surface. This arrangement permits a passenger with reduced mobility (e.g. a wheelchair user) to access the seat from an aisle through the partially exposed side of the footrest by sitting directly upon the seat pan and by then moving their legs into the seat unit via the exposed side of the footrest. This feature is not disclosed by Nicholas.

Instead, Nicholas discloses an arrangement wherein the seat is translated forward and then the leg rest is deployed to be coplanar with the seat pan and with a foot-supporting surface (see col. 12, lines 27 to 31 and Fig. 7c of Nicholas). In other words, the seat pan is spaced apart from the footrest/foot-supporting surface by at least the distance of the leg rest, and a person with reduced mobility has to sit on the leg rest before being able to move onto the seat pan - see Fig. 7c in particular.

Nicholas does not teach or suggest an arrangement in which the seat is movable to a position in which the seat pan is arranged contiguously with the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together form a surface, as required by present claim 1.

Furthermore, the arrangement of claim 1 is advantageous over Nicholas because claim 1 does not require a leg rest. Nicholas not only requires the seat to have a leg rest, but also requires that the leg rest be capable of bearing the full weight of a person sitting on the leg rest. The invention of claim 1 functions without a leg rest or with a stowable leg rest that is not able to support the full weight of a person. The invention of claim 1 therefore enables a simpler and lighter solution to the problem of providing persons having reduced mobility with access to a business class-type aircraft seat unit.

Nicholas, separately or in combination with any other cited reference, fails to anticipate or render obvious the subject matter of independent claims 1. Claims 1 is therefore allowable. As dependent claims depend directly or indirectly from the independent claim 1, they are also allowable at least based upon their dependency from allowable base claims, as well as features
they recite individually. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 102 and § 103 rejections be withdrawn and that these claims be allowed.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
